prompt.context: Our client is a drug store chain, similar to CVS. They are losing profits in the last few years.
prompt.question: Can you help us identify the reasons for the profit decline and suggest means to improve profits?

clarifying_info.q: What types of stores does the client operate?
clarifying_info.a: Stores are typical to CVS, located in several areas. They have pharmacy, health and beauty, and general merchandise departments.

clarifying_info.q: Can you tell me more about the store mix?
clarifying_info.a: 60% of the stores are located near hospitals, in areas with heavy competition, and in high-crime areas — these stores make a 10% loss. The remaining 40% of stores make 25% profits.

clarifying_info.q: What are the sales and profit margins by product type?
clarifying_info.a: Pharmacy: $20,000 sales per sq ft, 5% profit margin. Health and Beauty: $10,000 sales per sq ft, 20% profit margin. General Merchandise: $5,000 sales per sq ft, 10% profit margin.

framework: Revenue analysis: break down by store mix and product mix to identify where revenue/margin is under-performing
Cost analysis: assess whether costs (fixed, variable, COGS) have increased across store types or product lines
Store mix analysis: compare profitability of high-competition/high-crime hospital-adjacent stores vs. other locations
Product mix analysis: compare revenue per sq ft and margin across pharmacy, health & beauty, and general merchandise
Location factors: evaluate how proximity to hospitals, competition density, and crime rates affect store economics
Prioritize improvement levers: closing underperforming stores, shifting product mix toward higher-margin categories, improving location strategy

questions.prompt: Is the loss of profitability due to product mix, store mix, increasing costs, decreasing revenue, or a combination?
questions.guidance: A strong answer uses a structured breakdown: (1) Store mix — 60% of stores are loss-making (-10%), dragging down overall profitability despite 40% of stores performing well (+25%). (2) Product mix — Pharmacy generates the highest sales/sq ft but only 5% margin; Health & Beauty and General Merchandise have higher margins but lower sales volumes. The client may be over-indexed to pharmacy. (3) Candidate should identify it is likely a combination of store mix and product mix issues.

math.answer: Blended margin is only +4%, heavily dragged down by the 60% of underperforming stores

questions.prompt: What can the company do to improve profits?
questions.guidance: Candidate should focus deeply on one improvement area: (1) Change product mix — shift floor space from low-margin pharmacy toward higher-margin health & beauty or general merchandise. (2) Close or reposition bad stores — the 60% of loss-making stores are a structural drag; evaluate closing unprofitable locations or renegotiating leases. (3) Improve location strategy — avoid high-competition, high-crime, hospital-adjacent openings for future store expansion.

questions.prompt: What factors affect profitability of a particular store? (Additional brainstorm question)
questions.guidance: Candidate should generate a MECE list of store-level profitability drivers across revenue and cost dimensions.

brainstorming.prompt: What factors affect profitability of a particular store?

categories.name: Cost drivers
ideas: Rent and occupancy costs (hospital-adjacent or high-crime areas may command premium rents or require security spend)
Supply chain and inventory carrying costs

categories.name: Location factors
ideas: Proximity to hospitals (high foot traffic but also high competition)
Crime rate (raises security and shrinkage costs)

categories.name: Operational factors
ideas: Store layout and space allocation by department

recommendation: The client's profit decline is driven primarily by store mix (60% of stores are loss-making) and secondarily by product mix (over-reliance on low-margin pharmacy)
Prioritize closing or repositioning the 60% of underperforming stores in high-competition, high-crime, and hospital-adjacent locations
Reallocate floor space within profitable stores toward higher-margin health & beauty products
Revise the location strategy for new store openings to avoid structurally disadvantaged sites
risks: Closing stores may trigger lease penalties or community/reputational backlash
Reducing pharmacy presence may alienate customers who rely on it as a destination category
Shifting product mix away from pharmacy could reduce overall traffic
next_steps: Conduct store-level P&L analysis to rank closure candidates
Model margin impact of reallocating pharmacy sq ft to health & beauty
Assess lease obligations and exit costs for underperforming stores
Pilot product mix reallocation in 2-3 stores before chain-wide rollout
